title: What a REMS may require under 21 U.S.C. 355-1
subtopic: REMS elements and elements to assure safe use
rule_summary: Under 21 U.S.C. 355-1(a)(1), if FDA determines that a risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS) is necessary to ensure that the benefits of a drug outweigh its risks and informs the person who submits the application of that determination, that person shall submit a proposed REMS as part of the application. Under 355-1(e) FDA may require that a REMS include one or more additional elements if FDA makes the determination required with respect to each element: that the responsible person develop, for distribution to each patient when the drug is dispensed, a Medication Guide as provided for under 21 CFR Part 208 and, if FDA determines that it may help mitigate a serious risk of the drug, a patient package insert; that the responsible person conduct a communication plan to health care providers where FDA determines that the plan may support implementation of an element of the strategy; and, for a drug with a serious risk of an adverse drug experience occurring from an overdose or from abuse of the drug, that the drug be made available for dispensing to certain patients in unit dose packaging, packaging that provides a set duration, or another packaging system that FDA determines may mitigate the risk, or that the drug be dispensed to certain patients with a safe disposal packaging or safe disposal system if FDA determines that it may mitigate the risk and is sufficiently available. Under 355-1(f)(1) FDA may require that a REMS include such elements as are necessary to assure safe use of the drug, because of its inherent toxicity or potential harmfulness, if FDA determines that the drug, shown to be effective but associated with a serious adverse drug experience, can be approved only if, or would be withdrawn unless, such elements are required to mitigate a specific serious risk listed in the labeling, and, for a drug initially approved without elements to assure safe use, that other elements are not sufficient to mitigate the risk. Under 355-1(f)(3) elements to assure safe use shall include one or more goals to mitigate a specific serious risk listed in the labeling and may require that health care providers who prescribe the drug have particular training or experience, or are specially certified; that pharmacies, practitioners, or health care settings that dispense the drug are specially certified; that the drug be dispensed to patients only in certain health care settings, such as hospitals; that the drug be dispensed to patients with evidence or other documentation of safe-use conditions, such as laboratory test results; that each patient using the drug be subject to certain monitoring; or that each patient using the drug be enrolled in a registry. Under 355-1(f)(4) the elements described in (f)(3)(B), (C) and (D) may include a system through which the applicant is able to take reasonable steps to monitor and evaluate implementation of those elements by health care providers, pharmacists, and other parties in the health care system who are responsible for implementing them, and to work to improve implementation by those persons.
exam_relevance: Supplies the statutory menu from which each product-specific REMS is built, so that the elements that reach a dispensing pharmacy can be told apart from those addressed to prescribers, patients or the applicant.

authority.name: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act section 505-1, Risk evaluation and mitigation strategies

exceptions: An additional element under 21 U.S.C. 355-1(e) may be required only if FDA makes the determination required with respect to that element.
Elements to assure safe use may be required only on the determinations described in 21 U.S.C. 355-1(f)(1).
common_confusions: Treating every REMS as imposing pharmacy duties; pharmacy certification and dispensing conditions are elements that 21 U.S.C. 355-1(f)(3) permits a particular REMS to require.
Treating a Medication Guide as necessarily a REMS element; 21 U.S.C. 355-1(e)(2) makes it one element a REMS may require, and a Medication Guide is provided for under 21 CFR Part 208.
verification_notes: Read the current text of 21 U.S.C. 355-1(a)(1), (b)(1), (d), (e) and (f) on the Office of the Law Revision Counsel's United States Code site on 2026-09-14.
